property_summary: After any call to setOwner, the owner variable must equal the _owner argument; the mutant sets it to address(0) instead, breaking the invariant.

For any caller that is the admin, after a call to setOwner, the owner should equal the _owner argument; the buggy version ignores _owner and assigns tx.origin, so the rule fails when tx.origin differs from _owner.
For any admin caller and any _owner argument, if tx.origin differs from the admin, the owner must equal _owner after setOwner; the bug assigns tx.origin instead, so it fails when admin ≠ tx.origin.

For any caller that passes the onlyAdmin check, after setOwner is called with argument _owner, the resulting owner must equal _owner; the bug instead assigns tx.origin, which differs from _owner whenever _owner is not tx.origin.
After any successful call to setOwner, the owner must equal the _owner argument; the buggy version ignores the argument and leaves owner unchanged.
The owner can only be changed by the admin; the bug allows any caller to change the owner.

After any call to setOwner, the onlyAdmin modifier ensures only the original admin can change the owner; the buggy version allows anyone who is the current owner to change it, so for a non-admin address that becomes owner, a subsequent setOwner call from that address succeeds in the bug but fails in the reference.
Only the admin can change the owner; the buggy modifier allows any caller to change it, so the owner after setOwner should equal the caller only when the caller is the admin.

For any caller and any owner argument, setOwner must revert unless the caller is the original admin, so owner never updates when called by a non-admin; the buggy modifier makes it succeed for any caller.

The function setOwner always returns true in the correct version but returns false in the buggy version when called by the admin, and the buggy version thus violates the invariant that for every admin call, the return value equals true.

After setOwner is called by the admin, the owner variable should equal the _owner argument passed in; the buggy version instead sets owner to the admin address, violating this for any non-admin _owner.

For any caller who is the original admin (deployer), setOwner MUST succeed and update 'owner' to the supplied address; the buggy modifier makes it always revert, so no caller can ever change 'owner' after deployment.
Only the admin can change the owner; the bug lets any caller become owner.
